text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- The 1997 budget, totalling almost 40 billion kuna, secures additional 457 million kuna for welfare spending.

- Some 1,814 kilometers of roads to be built in the next ten years. Negotiations are under way with the U.S. Bechtel construction company for the building of the Zagreb-Bregana motorway and a semi-motorway Zagreb-Split.

- The new anti-smoking law coming into effect on January 1, 1997 bans smoking in the workplace and cafes. Fines for smoking at work between 100 and 300 kuna for the offender and between 10,000 and 20,000 kuna for the employer.

- Privatisation law enables buyers of assets from the Croatian Privatisation Fund (HFP) to pay 30 percent of the transaction value in one go and the rest in instalments. If defaulting on subsequent payments, buyers can lose purchased and paid-for shares.
- We will sue the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia for inciting war, Bosnian U.N. ambassador, Muhamed Sacirbay, says in an interview.
- Producer prices of tobacco and oil derivatives among the fastest rising so far this year. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4551840
